A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WMReward research and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D. All 22 pages were inspected; the appendix pages are visually identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original PhysicsIQ and VideoPhy experiments, human evaluations, computational measurements, ablations, and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds results for Wan2.2 and Sora2.

M1.justification: The VJEPA-2 surprise reward, sliding-window computation, guidance, BoN, and combined sampling procedures remain unchanged. Applying existing BoN sampling to additional generators does not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate PhysicsIQ image- and multiframe-conditioned generation and VideoPhy text-conditioned generation. The additional generators use these existing datasets and tasks; no new data domain or input scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Wan2.2 and Sora2 generator baselines and their reward-based comparisons; Table 3 adds Wan2.2. Existing comparators remain, including VideoMAE, Qwen2.5-VL, and Qwen3-VL. This extends the comparison set without changing the reward-baseline methodology.

E3.justification: The evaluated generator configurations expand to Wan2.2 and Sora2 using BoN. Table 1 explicitly states that Sora2's API prevents guidance. Existing metrics, sample counts, and search budgets remain unchanged, including 16 particles for PhysicsIQ and eight for VideoPhy.

E4.justification: The particle-scaling analysis, perceptual-quality evaluation, sampling-method comparison, and VJEPA size/window sensitivity experiments are retained. Appendix qualitative examples and failure analyses are identical. The new generator scores are ordinary benchmark comparisons.

E5.justification: Figure 1's scaling uncertainty bands and Table 4's runtime uncertainty reporting are retained. No repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: v2 adds PhysicsIQ I2V baseline/WMReward-BoN scores of 38.26/44.39 for Wan2.2 and 42.30/46.43 for Sora2, alongside alternative-reward results. Table 3 adds Wan2.2 VideoPhy results: overall physics consistency rises from 18.1 to 20.9 while semantic adherence falls from 63.5 to 55.2 with BoN. These are new configurations; matched pre-existing results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The numbered mathematical definitions and sampling derivations remain unchanged. v2 adds an unnumbered cosine-distance expression after Equation 6, restating its existing discrepancy term without introducing a new mathematical argument or formal property.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the claims about latent-world-model rewards, inference-time scaling, and improved physics plausibility without further training. The introduction's added Sora2 validation supplies evidence for these existing claims rather than redefining the contribution.

C2.justification: Table 1 adds the practical qualification that gradient guidance is unavailable for API-based Sora2. Interpretations of scaling, semantic-adherence tradeoffs, reward limitations, and failure mechanisms otherwise remain unchanged, including the discussion and Appendix D.

D1.justification: v2 adds a front-page code-access link and identifies Sora2's API constraint. Appendix A and Table 8 remain unchanged and do not provide corresponding generation settings for the newly evaluated Wan2.2 and Sora2 models.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to the Sora 2 system card, Jain et al.'s Diffusion Tree Sampling, and Park et al.'s SteerX. These modestly extend the generative-model and inference-time-alignment references without substantially changing the novelty argument.

P1.justification: The introduction and experimental overview receive localized revisions describing Sora2 and updating the I2V comparison. Date and code metadata also change. Section organization is retained, and much of the apparent textual movement results from page reflow.

P2.justification: Figure 1 adds Sora2 bars, legend entries, and a baseline reference line. Tables 1 and 3 gain model blocks, with additional table-formatting and placement adjustments elsewhere. The remaining figures and all appendix displays retain their content.

improvement.justification: The added Wan2.2 and Sora2 comparisons strengthen evidence that WMReward works beyond the original generators, including through an API, while retaining the earlier analyses and reporting the new VideoPhy tradeoff. The code-access link also improves documentation. These are limited gains: Appendix A does not document settings for the new generators, leaving their reproducibility less well supported.
